text:
sqlpipe exports PostgreSQL tables to Amazon S3 as Parquet files. It reads rows from a source database, converts them to columnar format, and writes the output to a bucket you specify. The tool handles schema mapping, compression, and partitioning automatically. It works with PostgreSQL 12 and later and writes files that Apache Spark, AWS Athena, DuckDB, and other analytics tools can read directly.

You can run sqlpipe on a schedule or as a one-time job. It supports incremental syncs: after the first full export, sqlpipe transfers only the rows that changed. This keeps transfer times short and storage costs low. A YAML configuration file controls the source connection, target bucket, and sync behavior.
